title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed, stencilled page, numbered '- 40 -' and 'n° 382', from a Bourbaki draft (rédaction) of the 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques. Fascicule de résultats'. That text appeared in 1967 and 1971, and Grothendieck took part in drafting it. He reused the sheet as scrap paper: it sits between handwritten notes on Tate's theorem and Hodge–Tate characters (previous page) and numerical fraction comparisons (next page). Only the archive's pencil foliation '56' is not typed.

The content, in modern terms:
(1) The fibre product of a transversal pair of morphisms f: X→S, g: Y→S exists as a manifold. Its tangent space at (x,y) is the fibre product of tangent spaces, {(h,k) ∈ T_xX × T_yY : T_x f(h) = T_y g(k)}.
(2) The projection g': X×_S Y → X is the pullback (base change) of g along f. If g is a submersion (resp. an immersion), so is g'.
(3) When X ⊂ S is a submanifold and f is the inclusion, transversality of (f,g) is the same as g being transversal to X. In that case f' identifies X×_S Y with the submanifold g^{-1}(X) of Y; in particular S×_S Y ≅ Y.
(4) 4.11.4 states the universal property of the fibre product in the category of manifolds.
(5) 4.12.1 defines Lie groups ('variétés de groupe') of class C^r over a complete valued field K. It also defines their morphisms, and records that:
- a Lie group is pure-dimensional;
- its underlying topological group is metrizable and complete;
- it is locally compact when K is locally compact.
The page serves foundational differential geometry for the Bourbaki series.
errors: In 4.11.4 the morphism j is denoted '(f,g)_S'. Since j is determined by u and v, the natural notation is (u,v)_S, so this is very likely a typing slip in the draft.

The statements on submersions, immersions and transversality are correct only with Bourbaki's definitions in the Banach setting, which require split images and kernels. Within that framework there is no real gap.

ideas.what: Fibre product of manifolds along a transversal pair; tangent space of the fibre product; universal property
ideas.modern_name: Transversal fibre products / pullbacks in the category of smooth (or analytic) manifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; Thom-era transversality, codified in Bourbaki's Variétés différentielles et analytiques
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats (1967), section on transversality and fibre products

ideas.what: Base change preserves submersions and immersions; for a submanifold, the fibre product equals the preimage g^{-1}(X)
ideas.modern_name: Stability of submersions under pullback; preimage of a submanifold under a transversal map

ideas.what: Lie groups over a complete valued field K and their morphisms; metrizability, completeness, local compactness
ideas.modern_name: Lie groups over R, C or p-adic fields (analytic groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lie, Cartan; Bourbaki; Serre's Lie Algebras and Lie Groups for the p-adic case
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats; Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. III

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of a Bourbaki draft reused as scrap paper. It contains only standard foundational material that was published in Bourbaki's Fascicule de résultats, and nothing on it is Grothendieck's own unpublished mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image. Note that the page is a typed Bourbaki draft ('n° 382'), not a handwritten note; only the foliation '56' is a pencil mark.
'(ce qui justifie...)' appears in the image as 'cé qui' (typing artefact), which is immaterial.
